fact: UNESCO's UPR 51st session contribution states that there is no legislation concerning freedom of information in Sao Tome and Principe and recommends introducing an access to information law.

Rádio Nacional reports that civil society (CIP, via Projeto Propalop) presented a draft access to administrative information law (anteprojeto) in October 2019, still unapproved, with no specific access to information law in force in São Tomé and Príncipe.
system: anteprojeto de lei de acesso à informação administrativa

fact: CIPSTP formally presented its draft access to information bill to Justice Minister Vera Cruz Cravid, who received it with interest.
system: draft Lei de Acesso à Informação

fact: CIPSTP states São Tomé and Príncipe has no public probity law and no access to information law, and asks the National Assembly to approve one by June 2026.
